name: Paychex (CIK 0000723531, FYE May-31, IBKR conid 272942, NASDAQ)
verdict: WATCH 5/10 (court 2026-08-02; sourcing 9 vacated to a fair-carry candidate, not an AI edge). The labor-leverage story is REAL but smaller and differently-caused than sourced: comp share of expenses 58->55->52% verifies exactly (FY26 10-K acc 0001193125-26-307785) but ~2/3 of the optic is denominator inflation (acquisition costs 0->162->304M + PEO pass-through) - comp/REVENUE fell only 218bp; the sourcing row's headcount years were TRANSPOSED (16,500 = FY24 pre-Paycor; 19,000 = FY25 post-Paycor) and like-for-like pro-forma revenue growth is +4.9% FY25->26, not +16.9%. The honest version - rev/employee +21%/2y on the pro-forma combined base (19,400->17,600 heads) - is genuine, but the filing attributes it to PAYCOR INTEGRATION, never to WISE ('600 AI features and agents' = verbatim, unaudited, zero cost/savings attribution = cannot bear model weight). The cleanest datum survives: cost of service revenue 28.03->25.71% with ALL $304M of acquisition costs in SG&A = +232bp genuine unadjusted gross-margin expansion (Paycor's standalone 65.9% gross margin made mix a HEADWIND, so legacy improvement exceeds it). Float test PASSES: only ~19% of the +129bp adjusted-margin expansion is float; ~81% real opex leverage, and FY27 float is guided DOWN ($195-205M vs $210.9M actual) while margin is guided UP. THE ADP PROBLEM APPLIES TO PAYX ITSELF: FY27 adjusted op margin ~44% is EXPLICITLY GUIDED (8-K 0001193125-26-280314) = the margin expansion is consensus by construction; the variant view must be a beat ABOVE 44%. Retention/NOW-seat: pricing is per-employee/per-check with 30-day cancellation - AI deflates PAYX's pricing unit via client EMPLOYMENT, not HR seats (partial insulation vs the NOW-seat problem), but payroll clients are FLAT at ~800k, retention pinned 82-83% three straight years, and the 10-K broadened its headline metric to '840,000 total customers' in the year the narrow one stopped growing (mild divergence, noted not flagged - the Paycor reconciliation itself is led with honestly). D6 = employment cycle: not currently adverse, structurally unhedged, no contractual floor. At ~19.5x FY27 guided adj EPS (~$5.95) vs own FY-end history 19.6-32.8x, the de-rate has already landed = RP_FAIR carry with a 3.9% yield at ~90% payout, mid-single-digit like-for-like growth.

court_scores.court: D1 2 / D2 1 (real leverage, Paycor-attributed, WISE unquantified) / D3 1 (per-employee unit = employment-geared; oligopoly-adjacent but ADP-style give-back live) / D4 0.5 (guided = priced; multiple at bottom of own band) / D6 neutral-now = 5/10; RP_FAIR path open

fv_note: bear = 17x flat $5.51 (employment downturn: per-employee revenue + worksite employees + insurance commissions hit simultaneously); base = ~20.3x FY27 guided adj ~$5.95; bull = ~23x on $6.10 (beat above the 44% guide - the only variant view that pays). Spot 116.33 = ~4% below base = FAIR. Edge ~0; carry = 3.9% yield + 7-9% guided adj EPS growth.
entry_plan: NO ENTRY on ai_adopter grounds (guided = priced; WISE unverifiable). RP_FAIR path: per fairly-paid-risk doctrine PAYX qualifies as deploying-book carry IF the book wants an hcm_payroll axis - fairness verified (bottom of own multiple band, float headwind absorbed in guide), tails bounded-not-eliminated (employment gearing, no floor, 90% payout), sleeve-cap $60k starter (NOT $120k - the D6 tail is macro-correlated with the consumer-credit axis $279k: both are employment-cycle books). Entry preference 105-115 tranched; do not chase above ~121 base. Axis interactions: business_services sleeve ($115k) + consumer-credit employment correlation - count PAYX against a combined employment-cycle budget.
d6_dominance: Employment cycle - revenue directly geared on three channels (PEPM/per-check, PEO worksite employees, insurance commissions on covered lives) with 30-day cancellation and no contractual floor. Not currently adverse (worksite employees +6% FY26), but it is the line that swamps a 232bp gross-margin story in any downturn. Float is a secondary D6: guided down, so FY27 margin quality is better than the headline.
retention_analysis: Per-employee/per-check pricing CONFIRMED verbatim. The NOW-seat problem applies at one remove: PAYX charges per employee PAID, not per HR seat - client HR-department AI adoption does not directly shrink the unit; aggregate client employment does. Competitive give-back is live (ADP guides gains away; PAYX current price realization positive via Paycor upmarket mix). Client count flat = all growth is price/penetration - sustainable only while the oligopoly holds pricing; retention 82-83% pinned means no evidence of pricing-power expansion.

self_red_team: RED: demanding a beat above the guided 44% may be too strict - PAYX guides conservatively, the float-down/margin-up construction means management is underwriting MORE opex leverage than the headline, and at the bottom of its own 20-year multiple band the employment tail is partially paid for; TINA doctrine says fair value IS the entry for quality. ANSWER: accepted in part - that is exactly why this is 5/10 WATCH with an open RP_FAIR path and a 105-115 band rather than AVOID; what it cannot be is an ai_adopter EDGE deployment, because the margin path is in the guide and the AI attribution is unverifiable - the Sep-29 print grades whether the conservative-guide reflex (frozen 0.65) beats the band discipline.
